title: Synthetic Anchorlet: calibration harness for cohort-driven quant acceptance
creator: Ava Patel
description: Build an automated harness ("Synthetic Anchorlet") that augments curated golden prompt cohorts with small, controlled synthetic perturbations and runs a probabilistic pass/fail gate for FP8/INT8 quantized rollouts. Goal: produce a reproducible, CI-friendly acceptance test that catches subtle semantic regressions introduced by mixed-precision kernels while keeping false positives low. The harness will: 1) expand golden cohorts with deterministic synthetic anchorlets (prefix masking, paraphrase swaps, numeric scaling, temperature perturbations) to exercise brittle edge-cases; 2) compute a small battery of fidelity signals (embedding cosine drift, token distribution JS divergence, top-k logit drift, BERTScore/BLEU for structured tasks) per sample and per-layer sensitivity metrics; 3) aggregate signals into a weighted acceptance score and expose a thresholded gate integrated with the rollouts service so that failed gates prevent canary promotion. Acceptance criteria: - end-to-end CI job that runs on PRs for quant-related changes (<= 2 hours wall time on the validation harness runner) - pass/fail gate decision produces deterministic result given seed - default gate thresholds tuned to match human-reviewed baseline (target false-positive rate <= 4%) - integration with telemetry dashboard and automatic alert when gate flips, including per-cohort breakdown and offending anchorlet examples.
comments: 2025-01-22 - Ava Patel: Initial RFC posted; motivated by recent INT8 canary that passed unit tests but showed semantic regressions in customer chat logs. Proposed synthetic anchors to amplify hard cases without needing customer data.

2025-01-28 - Carlos Mendez: Reviewed architecture. Main trade-offs: breadth of anchorlets (many types increases coverage but slows CI) vs. determinism. Proposal: keep sampled anchorlet types <= 4 per cohort and require deterministic seed in CI.

2025-02-02 - Design review (Priya Nair): Recommended curated 'anchor seed' UI for the console to let PMs add new golden seeds; flagged need for metadata tagging (task type, length band, templated vs. open-ended).

2025-02-06 - Eng sync: Decided metrics to compute: embedding_cosine_mean, embedding_cosine_median, token_jsdiv_mean, topk_logit_mean_shift, bertscore_f1_mean. Also add per-layer sensitivity probe: run short-layer ablation to get layer delta fingerprint for triage.

2025-02-10 - Carlos Mendez: PoC landed in branch github.com/redwood-inference/quant-acceptance/tree/eng/anchorlet-poc (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-acceptance/pull/182). PoC generates anchorlets, runs batch through float32 and int8-fp8 variants, computes metrics and uploads results to staging dashboard.

2025-02-12 - PM feedback (Lena Zhou): Request to add cohort-level pass_rate and a histogram of per-sample acceptance scores. Also wants a knob in the console to tune gate aggressiveness per release channel (canary/stage/prod).

2025-02-15 - Results snapshot: Baseline run on curated cohort of 600 prompts across ten cohorts: embedding_cosine_mean_drop: 0.0032, token_jsdiv_mean: 0.014, topk_logit_mean_shift: 0.021, bertscore_f1_delta_mean: -0.0065, overall_pass_rate: 96.4%. These numbers used to seed default thresholds.
2025-02-18 - Security (Maya Green): Confirmed no customer PII required; harness uses sanitized public/internal prompts only. No additional security review required at this stage.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for anchorlet generation to ensure deterministic outputs for a fixed seed. 2) CI job that runs float32 vs quantized model comparisons on a small fast cohort (smoke) and the full cohort overnight. 3) Human-in-the-loop review for any gate failures: collect top 20 failing examples, route to PM/Research triage. 4) Canary rollout integration: if gate passes, allow 5% canary traffic for 24h, monitor production fidelity metrics and auto-rollback if drift exceeds threshold.
metrics_definition: embedding_cosine_mean: mean cosine similarity between float and quantized response embeddings (lower is worse); token_jsdiv_mean: average JS divergence between token probability distributions over top-4096 tokens; topk_logit_mean_shift: mean absolute shift in top-5 logits normalized by temperature; bertscore_f1_mean: mean BERTScore F1 for reference-style tasks. Weighted_acceptance_score = 0.4*embedding_cosine_norm + 0.3*(1 - token_jsdiv_norm) + 0.2*berscore_norm + 0.1*(1 - topk_norm). Gate passes if Weighted_acceptance_score >= 0.88 on cohort median and cohort_pass_rate >= 94%.
rollout_policy: Default: passed gate -> promote to canary (5% traffic, 24h). Monitor production drift metrics; if production embedding_cosine_drop > 0.006 or cohort_pass_rate < 92% then auto-rollback. For high-risk customers (tagged in console), require manual approval even on pass.
next_steps: 1) Harden CI runner parallelism to get full cohort run under 2 hours (priority infra task). 2) Add console controls for gate aggressiveness per channel. 3) Expand anchorlet taxonomy with adversarial paraphrase generator from research (ENG-724000 planned). 4) Draft runbook for triage of failing gates.
notes: This harness is intentionally conservative: thresholds tuned to prioritize customer safety over aggressive compression wins. We'll iterate thresholds after 3 months of canary data. Determinism is critical for reproducible gating; ensure all randomness is seeded and logged.
